hot_days.label: Very hot days
hot_days.data_source: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) daily max temperature T2M_MAX, ~50 km grid
hot_days.definition: Days when the temperature reaches 35 °C (95 °F) or more.

story.happened: Very hot days: 198 days a year on average in 2001–2005, compared with 213 days a year in 2021–2025.
story.is_it_real: The trend is +8.2 days per decade (95% CI +5.3 to +11.2) and statistically significant (Mann-Kendall p < 0.001).
story.why_it_matters: Heat strains the heart and lungs; older adults and people with heart or lung disease are admitted to hospital more often during hot spells.
story.what_it_likely_means: This has been getting worse steadily. If the pattern holds, coming years are likely to look more like 2021–2025 than like the early years — or worse.

health_flag.text: Not good for asthma / COPD, heart disease and older adults (65+)

warm_nights.label: Warm nights
warm_nights.data_source: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) daily min temperature T2M_MIN, ~50 km grid
warm_nights.definition: Nights when the temperature stays at 20 °C (68 °F) or above.

story.happened: Warm nights: 214 nights a year on average in 2001–2005, compared with 227 nights a year in 2021–2025.
story.is_it_real: The trend is +6.0 nights per decade (95% CI +3.5 to +8.6) and statistically significant (Mann-Kendall p < 0.001).
story.why_it_matters: Warm nights stop the body recovering from daytime heat and disrupt sleep.
story.what_it_likely_means: This has been getting worse steadily. If the pattern holds, coming years are likely to look more like 2021–2025 than like the early years — or worse.

health_flag.text: Not good for heart disease and older adults (65+)

cold_days.label: Frost days
cold_days.data_source: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) daily min temperature T2M_MIN, ~50 km grid
cold_days.definition: Days when the temperature drops below 0 °C (32 °F).

story.happened: Frost days: none at all in any year from 2001 to 2025.
story.is_it_real: There is no change to test: the value was the same every year.
story.why_it_matters: Cold raises blood pressure and strain on the heart, and icy ground raises the risk of falls.
story.what_it_likely_means: This hasn't happened here in the whole record, so it isn't a concern for this place.

heavy_rain_days.label: Heavy rain days
heavy_rain_days.data_source: NASA POWER daily precipitation PRECTOTCORR, ~50 km grid
heavy_rain_days.definition: Days with 20 mm (0.8 in) of rain or more.

story.happened: Heavy rain days: 4 days a year on average in 2001–2005, compared with 4 days a year in 2021–2025.
story.is_it_real: The trend is +0.5 days per decade (95% CI -0.6 to +1.6), but not statistically significant yet (p = 0.34): it could still be normal year-to-year ups and downs. A longer record may settle it.
story.why_it_matters: Heavy rain raises flood risk: injuries, damp and mould at home, and trouble reaching medicines or care.
story.what_it_likely_means: No clear direction, so expect most years in the usual range of about 2–7 days.

source.name: US EPA — A Brief Guide to Mold, Moisture and Your Home

dry_days.label: Very dry days
dry_days.data_source: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) relative humidity RH2M, ~50 km grid
dry_days.definition: Days when average humidity is below 20%.

story.happened: Very dry days: 110 days a year on average in 2001–2005, compared with 106 days a year in 2021–2025.
story.is_it_real: The trend is -1.3 days per decade (95% CI -6.3 to +3.6), but not statistically significant yet (p = 0.83): it could still be normal year-to-year ups and downs. A longer record may settle it.
story.why_it_matters: Very dry air irritates the airways, eyes and skin, and can trigger coughing in people with asthma.
story.what_it_likely_means: No clear direction, so expect most years in the usual range of about 102–122 days.

source.name: US EPA — A Brief Guide to Mold, Moisture and Your Home

muggy_days.label: Muggy days
muggy_days.data_source: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) dew point T2MDEW, ~50 km grid
muggy_days.definition: Days when the dew point is 21 °C (70 °F) or higher — sticky, humid air.

story.happened: Muggy days: none at all in any year from 2001 to 2025.
story.is_it_real: There is no change to test: the value was the same every year.
story.why_it_matters: Long humid spells help mould and dust mites grow indoors, common asthma and allergy triggers.
story.what_it_likely_means: This hasn't happened here in the whole record, so it isn't a concern for this place.

source.name: US EPA — A Brief Guide to Mold, Moisture and Your Home

wettest_day.label: Wettest day of the year
wettest_day.data_source: NASA POWER daily precipitation PRECTOTCORR, ~50 km grid
wettest_day.definition: The most rain that fell in a single day each year.

story.happened: Wettest day of the year: 32 mm on average in 2001–2005, compared with 36 mm in 2021–2025.
story.is_it_real: The trend is +4.8 mm per decade (95% CI -4.2 to +13.7), but not statistically significant yet (p = 0.22): it could still be normal year-to-year ups and downs. A longer record may settle it.
story.why_it_matters: Bigger single-day downpours are what overwhelm drains and cause flash floods.
story.what_it_likely_means: No clear direction, so expect most years in the usual range of about 27–58 mm.

source.name: US EPA — A Brief Guide to Mold, Moisture and Your Home

pm25.label: Fine particle pollution (PM2.5)
pm25.data_source: NASA MERRA-2 aerosol diagnostics M2TMNXAER (monthly), PM2.5 rebuilt from dust, sea salt, sulfate, black and organic carbon, ~50 km grid
pm25.definition: Tiny particles in the air, 2.5 micrometres or smaller, from smoke, traffic, industry and dust.

story.happened: Fine particle pollution (PM2.5): 8.6 µg/m³ on average in 2001–2005, compared with 8.7 µg/m³ in 2021–2025.
story.is_it_real: The trend is +0.0 µg/m³ per decade (95% CI -0.1 to +0.1), but not statistically significant yet (p = 0.39): it could still be normal year-to-year ups and downs. A longer record may settle it.
story.why_it_matters: Fine particles reach deep into the lungs and blood and can trigger asthma attacks, COPD flare-ups and heart problems.
story.what_it_likely_means: No clear direction, so expect most years in the usual range of about 8.4–8.8 µg/m³.

source.name: US EPA — Air Cleaners and Air Filters in the Home

no2.label: Traffic & industry pollution (NO₂)
no2.data_source: NASA OMI/Aura tropospheric NO2 column OMNO2d (daily, 0.25° ≈ 25 km), 2005 onward
no2.definition: Nitrogen dioxide, a gas mainly from traffic, power plants and industry, measured from space by NASA's OMI instrument.

limits.source: none: there is no official health limit for satellite NO2 columns, so this card shows the trend only

story.happened: Traffic & industry pollution (NO₂): 3.11 ×10¹⁵ molec/cm² on average in 2005–2009, compared with 3.88 ×10¹⁵ molec/cm² in 2021–2025.
story.is_it_real: The trend is +0.49 ×10¹⁵ molec/cm² per decade (95% CI +0.47 to +0.51) and statistically significant (Mann-Kendall p < 0.001).
story.why_it_matters: NO₂ inflames the airways; long-term exposure is linked to asthma developing in children.
story.what_it_likely_means: This has been getting worse steadily. If the pattern holds, coming years are likely to look more like 2021–2025 than like the early years — or worse.

source.name: US EPA — Basic Information about NO2

fires.label: Wildfire activity nearby
fires.data_source: NASA FIRMS MODIS active fire detections (vegetation fires, confidence >= 30), 1 km
fires.definition: Wildfires and vegetation fires detected by NASA satellites within 50 km.

story.happened: Wildfire activity nearby: 29 fires a year on average in 2001–2005, compared with 65 fires a year in 2021–2025.
story.is_it_real: The trend is +18.4 fires per decade (95% CI +15.5 to +21.4) and statistically significant (Mann-Kendall p < 0.001).
story.why_it_matters: Wildfire smoke carries fine particles that worsen asthma, COPD and heart disease, and is a risk in pregnancy.
story.what_it_likely_means: This has been getting worse steadily. If the pattern holds, coming years are likely to look more like 2021–2025 than like the early years — or worse.

surface_heat.label: Neighborhood surface heat
surface_heat.data_source: NASA MODIS/Terra land surface temperature MOD11A2 (8-day, 1 km), via ORNL DAAC
surface_heat.definition: How hot the ground, roofs and roads get on summer afternoons, measured by NASA's MODIS satellite at 1 km.

story.happened: Neighborhood surface heat: 51.7 °C on average in 2001–2005, compared with 53.0 °C in 2021–2025.
story.is_it_real: The trend is +0.7 °C per decade (95% CI +0.5 to +0.9) and statistically significant (Mann-Kendall p < 0.001).
story.why_it_matters: Neighborhoods with more pavement and fewer trees stay hotter, raising heat stress for people living there.
story.what_it_likely_means: This has been getting worse steadily. If the pattern holds, coming years are likely to look more like 2021–2025 than like the early years — or worse.

heat_island.label: Hotter than surroundings by
heat_island.definition: How much hotter the area around the address is than the wider 11 × 11 km area.

story.happened: Hotter than surroundings by: 2.8 °C on average in 2001–2005, compared with 2.8 °C in 2021–2025.
story.is_it_real: The trend is -0.0 °C per decade (95% CI -0.1 to +0.0), but not statistically significant yet (p = 0.23): it could still be normal year-to-year ups and downs. A longer record may settle it.
story.why_it_matters: Urban heat islands add extra heat on top of the regional climate.
story.what_it_likely_means: No clear direction, so expect most years in the usual range of about 2.7–2.9 °C.
